label: verify-bm-mamou-mani-portfolio

claims.claim: The practice states the durable-vs-biodegradable contradiction; PLA is a 'middle ground' that only composts industrially.
claims.source_says: there is a contradiction between the idea of sustainable or durable and biodegradable, which is the opposite. The material we use, PLA, is a nice middle ground because it's not going to compost or degrade on its own
claims.note: Frederic, Altostrata page and Dezeen (60 C, 100% humidity) all say this.

claims.claim: No quantitative moisture/UV/creep/weathering data are published; durability evidence is only qualitative (Conifera outdoors, WOW!House 3 years unchanged, Altostrata weathering wording); only moisture sentence is about composting.
claims.source_says: Outside are more Conifera modules, deliberately exposed to wind and rain to prove the longevity of PLA
claims.note: The qualitative quotes are real, but the absence claim is a negative I could only spot-check on the pages named; the Altostrata page does mention humidity only for composting.

claims.claim: Fire is handled by additives per project (Roe fireproof, RIVA fire retardant, Fab.Shield) and no fire class or test result is published.
claims.source_says: The interior piece was 3D printed robotically from a blend of fermented sugar and non-toxic fire retardant.
claims.note: The three additive statements are confirmed (Fab.Shield: 'Flame-retardant blend developed for architectural performance requirements'); no class was seen on those pages, but absence is only spot-checked.

claims.claim: The only structural test on any practice page is one in-house pull test in an invalid unit (500 kg.m2); founder concedes PLA 'not very well researched'.
claims.source_says: Our in-house tests with ARUP and Fab Pub have proven a resistance to pull forces of 500 kg.m2. ... PLA although widely used in 3D printing is not very well researched
claims.note: Quotes are accurate, but 'only' is wrong: the Tate page reports load tests with Webb Yates Engineers and the Roe page says modules are structurally tested; the 'not well researched' line is page text, not attributed to the founder.

overall: Quotes are accurate. Claims 1 is supported. Claims 2 and 3 rest on absence of data, which was only spot-checked. Claim 4's 'only structural test' is overstated because the Tate page reports load tests.
